ai-at-work.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
ai-at-work.excerpt: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Anthropic's team got older and more senior, and now everyone's stuck in more meetings. This matters because it's a leading indicator of what happens when AI companies scale from scrappy startup to serious enterprise, and digital workplace pros need to watch this pattern play out across the sector. Here's the thing though: more senior people plus more meetings usually equals slower decision-making, and if there's one thing an AI company can't afford, it's moving at the speed of a traditional corporation.

ai-at-work.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says
ai-at-work.excerpt: Over the weekend, Masad clarified that OpenAI would replace Anthropic as its default model provider. Claude will still be available to customers on the platform.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Replit switched its default AI model from Anthropic's Claude to OpenAI, though Claude remains available as an option. This matters because it signals which AI tools are winning mindshare in developer communities, and your workplace tech stack decisions will increasingly follow these same competitive dynamics. After years of everyone treating Claude like the responsible choice, watching OpenAI reclaim default status is basically the AI equivalent of watching your favorite indie band get big and then wondering if they're still cool.

ai-at-work.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
ai-at-work.excerpt: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Mark Wahlberg says he's comfortable with AI in film as long as it enhances rather than replaces human work. This matters to digital workplace folks because it's the same tension playing out in every industry right now: workers wondering if AI is a tool or a threat. Here's the thing though: when a guy worth hundreds of millions says he's "open" to an AI clone carrying on his legacy, it's easy to be generous about the technology. Try telling that to the crew member whose job actually disappears.

ai-at-work.title: ServiceNow AI Control Tower: Selling a penthouse while building the frame
ai-at-work.excerpt: ServiceNow Inc. is making one of the more consequential and visible bets in enterprise artificial intelligence. The company says AI Control Tower can discover and govern any agent, work across models
ai-at-work.dwp_take: ServiceNow launched AI Control Tower, positioning it as a governance and cost management layer that can monitor AI agents across multiple platforms and models while enforcing policies. This matters because digital workplace leaders are terrified of AI sprawl and runaway costs, so anything claiming to wrangle that chaos gets attention. The irony is ServiceNow is essentially selling insurance for a problem that mostly exists in people's heads right now, but hey, sometimes the best products are solutions to fears that haven't fully materialized yet.

tools-tech.title: AI datacenter capex will far exceed forecast revenue through 2030
tools-tech.excerpt: Investors are pouring more into AI data center infrastructure than they can hope to recoup by 2030, according to Gartner. “Enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable
tools-tech.dwp_take: Tech companies are spending massive amounts building AI datacenters while the actual revenue those centers will generate through 2030 falls way short of covering those costs. This matters because it signals that AI infrastructure investment is partly speculative and partly driven by competitive panic, which means budgets for actual workplace AI tools and adoption will likely remain constrained. The dirty secret nobody wants to admit is that we're building a cathedral before we know what prayers people actually want to say in it.

tools-tech.title: Apple’s big AI week ends with Mac + Muse AI supercomputers
tools-tech.excerpt: <>Welcome to the week Apple showed us how serious it really is about artificial intelligence on Macs, with the company making more moves to deliver the tech in the most cost effective, responsible way
tools-tech.dwp_take: Apple spent the week announcing serious moves to get AI capabilities onto Macs in practical, cost-effective ways, positioning itself as the responsible player in workplace AI. For digital workplace pros, this matters because Mac-based AI tools could change how teams handle content creation, data analysis, and knowledge work without shipping everything to the cloud or waiting for external AI services. Honestly, if Apple actually delivers on the "responsible AI" promise without making us all subscribe to yet another service tier, they might actually have something here, though I'll believe it when I see it actually working in a real office.

tools-tech.title: Xbow spent $40K on AI and cracked Google Chrome wide open
tools-tech.excerpt: A chain of vulnerabilities in Google’s Chrome browser could have enabled researchers to take control of one billion Windows machines worldwide — and it cost them just $40,000 in AI compute time to dis
tools-tech.dwp_take: Xbow researchers spent forty grand in AI compute costs to uncover a critical Chrome vulnerability affecting a billion Windows machines, landing a quarter million dollar bug bounty from Google. This matters because your workforce is running Chrome on those machines right now, and the fact that AI can now find zero-days faster and cheaper than traditional methods means security is becoming an AI arms race. The real kicker: they made six hundred grand in profit after expenses, which tells you everything about how the economics of security have flipped upside down.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra: NVIDIA RTX Spark means business
tools-tech.excerpt: NVIDIA officially entered the Windows PC race this week, and its arrival brings a formidable new competitor to the premium AI PC market. With its RTX Spark platform, NVIDIA is bringing its Grace Arm C
tools-tech.dwp_take: NVIDIA just launched its RTX Spark platform for Windows laptops, bringing its Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU into the premium PC market, with Microsoft's new Surface Laptop Ultra as an early adopter. This matters because it finally gives enterprises a credible alternative to Intel and AMD for AI workloads, which means your procurement team needs to start thinking about how this changes your hardware refresh strategy. The real question isn't whether these laptops are fast, it's whether your organization's software actually runs on Arm architecture, and my guess is you're about to find out that answer the hard way.

digital-culture.title: ‘Parallel work’: How holding down multiple jobs at once shed its taboo
digital-culture.excerpt: Employees used to go to work and then come home. Now, they commonly go to one job and then to another. It’s called parallel work, and it essentially means taking on multiple jobs as opposed to having
digital-culture.dwp_take: More people are now openly juggling multiple concurrent jobs instead of hiding a side hustle, a shift that's shed the old stigma around working more than one gig at a time. For digital workplace leaders, this means rethinking policies around availability, communication tools, and work hours since your "full-time" employee might actually be splitting their brain between two or three organizations. Honestly, after thirty years watching knowledge workers, I'm surprised this took so long to normalize. The real question is whether your collaboration platform and meeting schedules can handle the chaos of truly distributed attention.

digital-culture.title: As employer burnout costs soar, EY gets at the heart of worker well-being with Vitality Index
digital-culture.excerpt: The tool is designed to help employers measure and boost workforce well-being.
digital-culture.dwp_take: EY launched the Vitality Index, a measurement tool aimed at helping employers track and improve employee well-being as burnout costs continue climbing. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because well-being initiatives need real data to succeed, and having a standardized way to measure vitality beats the usual gut-feel approach. That said, I've seen plenty of well-meaning indices and dashboards sit unused because nobody actually changed how work gets done, so the real test here is whether EY's tool leads to action or just becomes another number in the analytics pile.

industry-news.title: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27: Use One Number on Two iPhones
industry-news.excerpt: iPhone Handoff lets one phone number move automatically between two iPhones. Here’s how setup, carrier support, Apple Watch, Wallet, and eSIM switching work. The post iPhone Handoff in iOS 27: Use One
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple's new Handoff feature lets a single phone number seamlessly switch between two iPhones, which sounds convenient until you realize your boss now has even more ways to reach you across multiple devices. For digital workplace folks managing BYOD programs and mobile device policies, this is another complication because you're suddenly dealing with number portability and security considerations that didn't exist before. I've seen enough "just one more thing" Apple features tank workplace productivity, so good luck explaining eSIM switching to your IT security team when someone inevitably loses a phone.

industry-news.title: Nvidia Launches Three Nemotron AI Models, Including Two for Local AI Agents
industry-news.excerpt: Nvidia introduces three Nemotron AI models, including a 120B-parameter system and two smaller Bolt models designed for local AI agents and enterprise tasks. The post Nvidia Launches Three Nemotron AI
industry-news.dwp_take: Nvidia just dropped three new Nemotron AI models, including a hefty 120-billion parameter version and two smaller Bolt models meant to run locally on enterprise hardware. This matters because digital workplace leaders are getting real options for deploying AI without shipping every conversation to a cloud vendor's servers, which means better privacy, lower latency, and potentially fewer regulatory headaches. Honestly, the local AI agent story is finally getting interesting, assuming enterprises can actually figure out how to run these things without their IT teams losing their minds over GPU requirements.

industry-news.title: Sony Wants Audiophiles to Pay $5,900 for Its New Gold-Plated Walkman
industry-news.excerpt: Sony's new gold-plated Walkman costs $5,900 and promises premium audio. Here's what its upgraded hardware offers and whether it's worth the price. The post Sony Wants Audiophiles to Pay $5,900 for Its
industry-news.dwp_take: Sony just dropped a $5,900 gold-plated Walkman aimed at serious audio enthusiasts who want their portable music player to look as expensive as it sounds. For digital workplace folks, this is a reminder that premium hardware still exists in a world obsessed with cloud-based everything, and some professionals genuinely need better tools than the company-issued earbuds. Personally, I'd rather spend that money on noise-canceling headphones that actually work in open offices, but hey, if you're mixing tracks on the train, maybe gold plating does something magical.

industry-news.title: iPhone Duo Camera Tricks: Smart Take, Kid Cue, Duo Preview, and More
industry-news.excerpt: Apple's iPhone Duo introduces Smart Take, Kid Cue, Duo Preview, and Duo FaceTime. Here's how its folding design changes group photos and where its cameras fall short. The post iPhone Duo Camera Tricks
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple's new iPhone Duo foldable phone includes camera features like Smart Take, Kid Cue, and Duo Preview that leverage its unique dual-screen design to improve group photos and video calls. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because hybrid work still relies heavily on video conferencing and remote collaboration, so any hardware that makes group calls less awkward is worth paying attention to. That said, calling these camera tricks a workplace game-changer feels like a stretch when most companies are still figuring out how to make their existing video setup not look like a hostage situation.
